case_name: Pinaki Chatterjee and Others v Central Administrative Tribunal and Others
facts: Pinaki Chatterjee and Others v Central Administrative Tribunal and Others
No. 2053 of 2009 (Arising out of S.L.P. (C) No. 12687 of 2003)
The right of the appellants herein, if any, to be regularized in Class 'C' Services of the Railways is the question involved in this appeal
Appellants were directly appointed in Group 'C' posts except serial No.5 in the Electrical Department of the Railway Electrification Project.
As despite working for a long time, their services were not regularized, they filed two original applications before the Central Administrative Tribunal, Patna, Circuit Bench, Ranchi

By reason of a judgment and order dated 5.7.2001, the said original applications were allowed, in part, directing: 'In the result, the applicants' claim to be regularized in Group 'C' post as asserted in the OAs in hand is not acceptable, instead they were required to be regularized in feeder cadre in Group-'D' post by providing pay protection of 'C' post.'
Appellants aggrieved thereby filed a writ petition in the High Court of Jharkhand at Ranchi.

The said writ petition has been dismissed by reason of the impugned judgment, stating: 'No doubt, the petitioners were casually employed in Grade-C initially and thereafter they acquired temporary status, but the fact remains, and the finding of the fact by the Tribunal is, that the selections of the petitioners were not regular selections.'

It was urged that the Tribunal and consequently, the High Court committed a serious error in opining that the posts in Group 'C' in the Central Government were required to be filled up only through promotion and not through direct recruitment.

The learned counsel would also contend that from a letter dated 25.8.1997, which was issued by way of a representation made by the appellants to the General Manager, Central Organisation, Railway Electrification, Allahabad, it would appear that they had, except one, were directly appointed in the posts of T.C.M. Electrician Fitter, W/Driver Grade 'C' posts.
Learned counsel would contend that it is also not a case where the appellants do not possess the requisite qualification.
They had also passed the trade test.
It was furthermore urged that the Patna High Court in a similar situation having granted relief, the Jharkhand High Court committed a serious error in refusing to grant the same.
issues: The right of the appellants herein, if any, to be regularized in Class 'C' Services of the Railways

Whether the Tribunal and consequently, the High Court committed a serious error in opining that the posts in Group 'C' in the Central Government were required to be filled up only through promotion and not through direct recruitment.
Whether the appellants possess the requisite qualification for regularization in Group 'C' posts.
petitioner_arguments: The right of the appellants herein, if any, to be regularized in Class 'C' Services of the Railways

The Tribunal and consequently, the High Court committed a serious error in opining that the posts in Group 'C' in the Central Government were required to be filled up only through promotion and not through direct recruitment.
The appellants possess the requisite qualification for regularization in Group 'C' posts.
respondent_arguments: The Railway Electrification was a temporary project
The posts held by the appellants, indisputably, were purely on a casual basis and not against any cadre post.

Appellants have not been appointed upon compliance of the provisions of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India and/or the recruitment rules framed under the proviso appended to Art. 309 of the Constitution of India.
court_reasoning: The question, however, which arises for consideration is as to whether in the peculiar facts and circumstances of this case, the High Court should have directed regularization of the services of the appellants.
It has not been denied or disputed that Railway Electrification was a temporary project.
As noticed hereinbefore, the posts held by the appellants, indisputably, were purely on a casual basis and not against any cadre post.

Appellants furthermore have not been appointed upon compliance of the provisions of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India and/or the recruitment rules framed under the proviso appended to Art. 309 of the Constitution of India.
holding: The High Court should not have directed regularization of the services of the appellants.
The Railway Electrification was a temporary project
The posts held by the appellants, indisputably, were purely on a casual basis and not against any cadre post.

Appellants have not been appointed upon compliance of the provisions of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India and/or the recruitment rules framed under the proviso appended to Art. 309 of the Constitution of India.
